reachable: Yes, on both counts. (a) At scoring: cups_probe._fwd_pred calls net(tok, types, key_pad) — the arch's forward — and reads pred[rpos]. rpos = 2*r is a command position, and the pointer contribution is added to pred[:, 0::2] and masked by valid_cmd, so it lands exactly on the scored read. I confirmed on a padded, build_cups_layout-shaped batch: perturbing ptr_out.weight from zero changes |pred| at the read position by 0.17-0.21 and by exactly 0.0 at observation positions and on the padded tail. Causality holds: perturbing an observation token moves predictions only at positions >= it. (b) In training: at init ptr_out is zeroed, so contrib is exactly zero and the forward is bit-identical to r22 (verified: all inherited params equal, pred/h maxdiff 0.0). At that point ptr_out.weight/bias are the ONLY pointer parameters with nonzero gradient (all others measured exactly 0.0); once ptr_out leaves zero every pointer parameter receives gradient (ptr_addr 4e-5, ptr_move 6e-5, ptr_gate 1e-4, codebook 7e-6, tau 1e-5, unbind 2e-8 in one measured batch). So the mechanism bootstraps through a single zero-init readout — reachable, but with a one-step delay and a notably tiny gradient on ptr_unbind. Cost: +13% wall time per fwd+bwd vs r22 on CPU at B=32, L=64 (467 vs 414 ms), consistent with the hypothesis's 'same order' claim (which it flagged as unmeasured).
solves_outside_model: No. The arch's forward consumes only (tok_emb, types, key_pad) — it never receives command strings, step metadata or the `mv` text, and there is no import or call path that could supply them; I read the whole 155-line file and grepped it. Every quantity in the pointer table is derived from the frozen embeddings the model already sees: addresses are a learned linear map of the command embedding, values are the raw observation embeddings, and the routing is a learned softmax whose temperature, existence gate, unbinding strength and null bias are all trained parameters. The retraction shape (Python resolving the chain and stamping the answer into the read token) cannot occur here for a second reason: the genome's stream is baseline_interleave, which exposes no code_cmds, so command tokens are the raw standardized embeddings in both the native and role-swapped arms and the read token is identical across arms by construction. I also grepped the other selected chunks (r2_shrunk_zca target, r12 objective, r6 batcher, r18 head/optim) for string parsing — none touch command text; the r18 head mines its triples from embedding cosines. My own reachability probes parse `mv` strings, but those are throwaway scripts in /tmp, not part of the candidate.
summary: The code is a faithful implementation of its hypothesis. I checked each mechanical claim by execution and all of them hold: bit-identical to r22 at init (all inherited params equal, pred/h maxdiff exactly 0.0, because the new modules are constructed after super().__init__ and ptr_out is zero-init); one address head, quotiented against a Gram-Schmidt-orthonormalized learned codebook and unit-normalized; items matched only against strictly earlier addresses with a learned temperature, a log-existence bias and a null slot; read taken BEFORE the addresses are updated; src = unit(sum w_j a_j), dst = unit(g - lambda*<g,src>*src) with lambda = sigmoid of a learned scalar; addresses dragged by mu_i * w_ij toward dst while values are never rewritten; ex_j = (1-mu_j)*live_j with mu read off the causal trunk state; injection through a sigmoid gate over trunk state plus exactly the three named scalars (mass, peak, read RMS) and a zero-init (D,D) readout; parent's renderer, path-state memory, transition readout and transition_from_emb untouched. Driving the real _pointer_route with idealized additive path codes routes the correct content at depths 1-4 (cos 1.000 to the routed content, near 0 to the others), so the transport arithmetic composes as described. I then went past the author's jail limit and measured the superposition premise they flagged as unmeasurable, using the repo's own frozen encoder: it holds single-hop — with the module's untrained pipeline, an mv command's code matches its source path at +0.39 cosine versus ~0.00 for other paths, and Gram-Schmidt unbinding recovers the destination path top-1 in 33/50 (chance 2.6%); a 96-d projection costs little (34/50 vs 42/50 at 768-d). The mv->mv chain link is strong (37-40/40 at hop 2). The weak point is the last link, read-command against an mv-residual address: 28/40 at depth 3 and 23/40 at depth 4 against chance 13/40, and end-to-end with oracle move gates the routed content is picked 15/30 (depth 3) and 8-10/30 (depth 4) against chance 7.5/30. So the mechanism carries real signal from the actual geometry, but 'composes by construction' overstates its strength exactly in the eligible depth-3/4 slice; the design needs learning to sharpen it, which is what the author's own failure-mode list says. Nothing computes the routing outside the model. Four minor wording divergences, no material or fatal ones. Not checked: whether the fixed step budget actually separates mu on moves versus reads, learns the quotient basis, tau, lambda and the injection gate (needs a real training run); real windows also move several contents and interleave ctx and non-cups commands, which my single-mover probes did not model; GPU wall clock (CPU only); and I never ran the scoring pipeline end-to-end since no trained net was available. Repo untouched (git status clean), nothing installed, all work in the session scratchpad.

divergences.claim: "One affine head maps the raw pooled command embedding to a ptr_dim code" (hypothesis step 1).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code applies a LayerNorm first: g = _quotient(ptr_addr(ptr_ln(cmd_raw)), basis). LayerNorm is a per-vector nonlinearity (division by that vector's std), so the map is not affine. I measured whether this breaks the additivity premise the mechanism rests on: it does not. With the module's own init pipeline on real encoder embeddings, sim(mv-code, its source path code) = +0.392 with LN vs +0.392 without, and Gram-Schmidt unbinding identifies the destination path top-1 33/50 either way.

divergences.claim: "interleaves `mv <src> <dst>` steps whose observation is the EMPTY string" and "a step the model judges to be a move contributes no content item (its observation is empty)" (hypothesis lines 7-8, step 5).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The mv output text is indeed '' in the data, but render_obs wraps it as 'cwd=... exit=0\n' and the pooled+standardized embedding is a present, nonzero constant vector — it is placed into vals[j] unchanged. Nothing zeroes it. The only suppression is ex_j = (1-mu_j)*live_j; at init ptr_move.bias = 0 so mu = 0.5 for EVERY command and every move item enters the read with existence 0.5. Whether move items stop polluting the read depends entirely on the learned gate, not on the observation being empty.

divergences.claim: "Depth composes for a structural reason, not a learned coincidence ... One head serving both roles is what makes dst(i) and src(i+1) agree by construction rather than by luck."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code does implement exactly the described construction, and the mv->mv link is strong on real embeddings even with an UNTRAINED address head: at hop 2 the transported address beats both unmoved exposures 37-40/40 (chance 1/3), mean margin +0.61. But the final link — the read command `cat <final path>` matching an address that is now an mv-residual — is weak precisely in the eligible slice: 28/40 at depth 3 and 23/40 at depth 4 (chance 13/40), mean margin +0.21 / +0.17. End-to-end through the real _pointer_route with oracle move gates and real embeddings, the routed content is picked 15/30 at depth 3 and 8-10/30 at depth 4 (chance 7.5/30). So the agreement is approximate and degrades over hops; 'by construction' overstates the strength at the depths that are actually scored. All of this is a lower bound (the head, quotient basis, tau, lambda and gates are learned), and the author lists the superposition premise and soft-match diffusion as failure modes — but the body text asserts structure where the measurement shows a compounding approximation.
